thread.title: Stocks Open Mixed; Amazon Eyes $1 Trillion, Tilray Lights Up Pot Stocks

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Open Mixed; Amazon Eyes $1 Trillion, Tilray Lights Up Pot Stocks
text:
Stocks opened in tense, mixed trade Wednesday as global markets set up in a holding pattern ahead of a Friday deadline for trade talks between the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
X
An analyst price-target hike lifted Google-parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ), and pointed Amazon.com ( AMZN ) above $1 trillion in market capitalization. Tilray ( TLRY ) triggered a cannabis rally with its second-quarter report, while Dick's Sporting Goods ( DKS ) and cloud stock Box ( BOX ) dived after their quarterly results.
The Nasdaq Composite led, opening up 0.2% as both Amazon and Alphabet pulled higher. The S&P 500 managed a 0.1% gain. The Dow Jones industrial average dipped to a narrow loss, with American Express ( AXP ) posting the index's heaviest decline. ( For updates on this story and other market coverage, visit the Stock Market Today .)
A positive revision to GDP growth data had little impact on early trade. The Commerce Department revised its second-quarter GDP growth estimate higher, to 4.2%, vs. its original 4.1% growth estimate. Economists had forecast a reduction to a 4% gain. The GDP price index inflation gauge remained unchanged, up 3%.
Trade War: Negotiators Face Deadline Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland dived into talks with U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and with Mexican Economy Minister Ildefonso Guajardo late Tuesday. The talks were scheduled to continue Wednesday morning ahead of what the U.S. said is a hard-and-fast Friday deadline to complete a deal.
Canada had been shut out of the early rounds of U.S. talks with Mexico, but Freeland said the U.S.-Mexico agreement reached was generally positive for Canada, particularly in terms of Mexico's labor concessions. President Trump has threatened to apply tariffs to Canada's U.S. auto imports if a deal is not reached, and has said the U.S. could move forward with a Mexico-only trade deal. Once the White House notifies Congress that a deal is signed, there is a 90-day waiting period before the deal can be formalized. The White House is trying to push through a deal before a new administration takes control in Mexico on Dec. 1.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Global Markets: China Mixed, Europe In The Red In Asia, China's markets posted a mixed finish with Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index up 0.2% and the Shanghai Composite taking a 0.3% loss. The Hang Seng is up 2.7% for the week, and back above its 50-day moving average as it rebounds from a two-month decline.
In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 added 0.2%, moving it within 1% of its high for the year, set in May.
Europe's markets improved to mixed action in afternoon trade. London's FTSE 100 remained down 0.4%, while Frankfurt's DAX and the CAC-40 in Paris each climbed 0.2%.
Amazon Eyes $1 Trillion, Threatens Roku; Tilray Leads Pot Stocks Amazon.com rose 1.2% to run ahead of the FANG stock tech leaders in early trade. Morgan Stanley kept its overweight rating on the stock, while hoisting its price target 35%, to 2,500. At that price, Amazon would reach $1.2 trillion in market capitalization. It would be only the second company, following Apple ( AAPL ), to reach that milestone. The note cited Amazon's improving business mix, which is producing high-growth, high-margin revenue, and free cash flow to invest back into the business. Shares of the IBD Leaderboard stock are extended after clearing a three-weeks tight pattern in early August.
In another piece of Amazon news, Roku ( ROKU ) tumbled more than 3% lower following news reports that Amazon was preparing to launch an ad-supported free video service. The service would target the 48 million users of Amazon Fire tablet devices, and would be somewhat similar to the Roku Channel, which airs TV reruns and older movies. The channel has reportedly become a profit center for Roku.
Morgan Stanley also hiked its price target for Google-parent Alphabet, sending shares 1% higher in opening trade. The report based the new price target of 1,515 on improving results at the company's Waymo self-driving car unit. The unit could grow to $175 billion in value, up from current estimates at $45 billion, as the company expands its ride-sharing, logistics and licensing businesses. Alphabet shares remain in a buy range, above a 1,201.59 handle buy point.
Tilray torched up the cannabis sector, rocketing 13% higher after reporting a 95% surge in second-quarter revenue. Losses widened to 14 cents per share , below analyst targets. The stock has spiked 51% for August, through Tuesday's session. Other weedy stocks also rose: Cronos ( CRON ) surged 5%, while Canopy Growth ( CGC ) added 1.5%.
On the downside, Dick's Sporting Goods dived 7% and Box folded 11% following their earnings results.
After Wednesday's close, Salesforce.com ( CRM ) and retailer At Home Group ( HOME ) are scheduled to report quarterly results.
